_about.what: Literature stream for the weights: for each question type, an evidence class for each dimension, taken from textbooks, papers and NASA records. scoring/derive_literature_weights.py turns the classes into the 51 AHP pairwise judgements (scoring/literature_judgements.csv) and their weights (scoring/literature_weights.json).

classes.1: decisive: the cited sources show that this condition alone can decide the outcome of the question type (burns or not, detected or not, extinguished or not) within habitat ranges
classes.2: strong modifier: the sources report a quantified or clearly documented change in the outcome, but not an on-off effect within habitat ranges
classes.3: weak or not documented: no source in this list documents an effect of this condition on the outcome of the question type

_about.rule: Pairwise judgement from the class difference, on Saaty's verbal scale: same class 1 (equal), one class apart 3 (moderately more important), two classes apart 5 (strongly more important).

The classes were assigned by an AI session from the cited findings. They are not judgements of people; review by combustion researchers is the next step.
_about.source_ids: References are listed in scoring/BUILDUP.md section 7. A dagger in 'checked' means the finding was checked only in an abstract or a secondary source.

prevention.outcome: whether a solid material ignites and spreads a flame, and how fast

o2.finding: A solid burns only above a limiting oxygen concentration (the oxygen index; NASA's maximum oxygen concentration). In microgravity the flammability map in oxygen against flow has a low-oxygen limit. Oxygen can therefore decide whether a material burns at all.

flow.checked: C7 abstract (dagger); C8 yes; PSI-25 record
flow.finding: In microgravity, flow decides burning near the limits: flames quench at low flow (radiative loss) and blow off at high flow, with a flow of maximum flammability between. BASS-II names airflow speed and oxygen as its main variables.

fuel.finding: Materials differ by an order of magnitude in flammability: heat release capacity about 460 to 510 J/(g K) for PMMA against 35 for PTFE, 52 for Nomex and 25 for a polyimide.

pressure.finding: Lower total pressure raises the oxygen threshold of solids: for PTFE from about 42% at 101.3 kPa to about 53% at 48.2 kPa. The shift is quantified, and smaller than the range of oxygen fractions habitats use.

geometry.checked: citations yes; content not checked in the text (dagger)
geometry.finding: Thermally thin and thick fuels spread in different regimes (theory of opposed-flow flame spread), and large samples burn differently from the small samples of standard tests.

role.finding: Evidence on a different outcome is indirect evidence (outcome indirectness). 16 of the 24 catalog investigations measured a flammability-related outcome (flame spread, ignition, extinction limit, burning rate), so a purpose mismatch is a real but not decisive gap for prevention.

detection.outcome: how much smoke a fire or an overheated material makes, its particle size, and whether detectors respond

role.finding: Only a study that measured smoke or detector response gives direct detection evidence; another outcome is indirect evidence. 10 of the 24 catalog investigations measured smoke, soot or detection.

fuel.finding: Detector response depends on the material: in the SAME flights the ionization detector often missed the small smoke particles of Teflon and Kapton.

flow.finding: Smoke transport and particle growth depend on flow and residence time: low velocities and little mixing in microgravity favour larger particles.

o2.finding: No source in this list documents an oxygen effect on the smoke of overheated materials. SAME made its smoke by heating samples, not by burning them.

pressure.finding: No source in this list documents a pressure effect on smoke or detector response.

geometry.finding: No source in this list documents an effect of sample shape on smoke or detector response.

suppression.outcome: whether a flame is extinguished, and at which oxygen or agent level

role.finding: Only a study that tested extinguishment gives direct suppression evidence (outcome indirectness). BASS and FLEX state the effectiveness of gaseous agents as an objective.

o2.finding: A flame exists only above its limiting oxygen index: about 0.12 for methanol and 0.15 for heptane droplets in O2/N2 on the ISS. CO2 extinguishes methane flames when their maximum temperature falls to about 1600 K.

fuel.finding: The limiting oxygen index differs by fuel: about 0.12 for methanol against 0.15 for heptane.

diluent.finding: The agent shifts the limit moderately: methanol's limiting oxygen index goes from about 0.12 in N2 to about 0.14 with CO2 added, and at 21% O2 more CO2 slightly lowered the extinction diameter.

flow.finding: Flow changes extinction in microgravity: radiative extinction at low flow, blowoff at high flow.

pressure.finding: Lower total pressure raises the oxygen threshold of solids (PTFE about 42% to 53% from 101.3 to 48.2 kPa).

geometry.finding: BASS assessed the agent over different geometries, but no source in this list gives the size of the effect.
